title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page has nothing to do with motives. It is page 5 of a Bourbaki typescript draft, 'rédaction n°370', on Haar measure: the material of Bourbaki, Intégration, ch. VII, §1. Grothendieck evidently reused the sheet (it is scanned upside down) as the backing or scrap paper of his 1965 motive notes. Its content is Bourbaki's, not his.

The mathematics is routine:
(1) Setting. A locally compact group G acts on the right on a locally compact space X by δ(s)x = x s^{-1}.
(2) Relatively invariant measures. A measure μ on X is relatively invariant if δ(s)μ = χ(s)μ for all s, where δ(s)μ is the image measure. The function χ is the multiplier, a continuous character G → R_{>0}.
(3) Equivalent forms. Unwinding the definition gives ∫ f(xs) dμ(x) = χ(s)^{-1} ∫ f dμ and μ(As) = χ(s)μ(A).
(4) Opposite group. Viewing the action as a left action of the opposite group G°, μ is relatively invariant for G° with the same multiplier.
(5) A group acting on itself. G acts on itself by left translation γ(s)x = sx and by right translation δ(s)x = x s^{-1}. This yields the notions of left- and right-invariant, relatively invariant and quasi-invariant measures. Forward references to n°s 8 and 9 presumably cover the existence and uniqueness of Haar measure and the modular function.
(6) Inversion. Since x ↦ x^{-1} is a homeomorphism, one defines f̌(x) = f(x^{-1}) and μ̌(f) = μ(f̌) for f in K(G). Hence ∫ f dμ̌ = ∫ f(x^{-1}) dμ, and μ̌(A) = μ(A^{-1}) for μ̌-integrable sets A.

This is standard preparatory material leading to the Haar measure and the modular function.
errors: None found. Formulas (7'), (8') and (9') are mutually consistent with δ(s)x = x s^{-1} and δ(s)μ the image measure. For example, μ(As) = ∫ 1_A(x s^{-1}) dμ = χ(s)μ(A), and ∫ f(xs) dμ = χ(s^{-1}) ∫ f dμ = χ(s)^{-1} ∫ f dμ.
